rationale: Ileocolonoscopy as the reference standard for postoperative recurrence surveillance operationalizes the therapeutic goal of thiopurine prophylaxis by providing the monitoring endpoint.
The SIBO epiphenomenon principle extends the CD antibiotics argument: both reject simple antimicrobial-only strategies in favor of addressing root causes.
ACG UC 2019's strong recommendation against thiopurine monotherapy for induction supports AGA UC 2020's conditional recommendation against the same.
ACG's recommendation against methotrexate for UC maintenance supports AGA's broader recommendation against methotrexate for both induction and maintenance.
ACG's strong recommendation for infliximab-thiopurine combination supports AGA's conditional recommendation for biologic plus thiopurine induction.
ACG specifies the post-cyclosporine rescue context, extending AGA's general thiopurine maintenance recommendation with a concrete clinical scenario.
ACG's strong recommendation against thiopurine induction supports ECCO's weak recommendation against thiopurine monotherapy for induction.
AGA's conditional recommendation against thiopurine induction supports ECCO's weak recommendation against thiopurine monotherapy for induction.
AGA's affirmation of thiopurine maintenance extends ACG's induction rejection by clarifying that thiopurines retain a role in maintenance despite being unsuitable for induction.
ACG's strong high-quality recommendation for anti-TNF induction supports ECCO's strong moderate-quality recommendation for the same indication.
ACG's strong recommendation to continue anti-TNF for maintenance supports ECCO's strong recommendation for anti-TNF maintenance after induction.
ECCO's VARSITY-based preference for vedolizumab over adalimumab extends AGA's ranking of infliximab/vedolizumab above adalimumab with head-to-head trial evidence.
ACG's strong recommendation for vedolizumab in post-anti-TNF patients extends AGA's conditional recommendation ranking ustekinumab/tofacitinib above vedolizumab for TNF-exposed patients.
ACG's strong recommendation for tofacitinib after anti-TNF failure extends AGA's broader conditional recommendation for the post-TNF class by confirming tofacitinib's specific role.
ECCO's VARSITY-based evidence that vedolizumab is superior to adalimumab supports ACG's strong recommendation for vedolizumab in the post-anti-TNF setting.
The SONIC trial's demonstration of combination therapy superiority provides direct evidence supporting the clinical utility of azathioprine for maintaining remission.
Yamada's observation that biologics replaced corticosteroids as cornerstone extends Steinhart's account of steroid dominance by describing the therapeutic paradigm shift.
The critique of the step-up pyramid supports the observation that biologics have not altered the high surgical rate, reinforcing the case for earlier aggressive therapy.
Therapeutic drug monitoring operationalizes anti-TNF therapy by optimizing drug levels to sustain the remission that infliximab has been proven to achieve.
ECCO's structured FC monitoring protocol operationalizes the diagnostic utility of fecal calprotectin by extending it from one-time IBS/IBD differentiation to longitudinal relapse surveillance.
ACG's four-domain severity framework extends ECCO's endoscopy/imaging requirement by adding patient-reported outcomes, inflammatory burden, and disease impact.
The AGA guideline's discussion of intensive infliximab dosing extends ACG's standard IV steroid protocol by addressing rescue therapy when corticosteroids fail in ASUC.
The clinical observation that most IBD patients have extensive antibiotic histories supports the broader claim that Western lifestyle factors drive microbial diversity loss linked to disease.
Pimentel's description of emulsifiers disrupting mucous membranes provides a specific mechanistic pathway supporting Chutkan's claim about processed-food-driven microbial diversity loss.
The clinical antibiotic-IBD link extends the BioEssays craving-manipulation hypothesis by identifying antibiotic-driven dysbiosis as a trigger for bacterial manipulation of host eating behavior.
